provenance.description: GS1 DataMatrix / Data Matrix ECC 200 vectors for M6: gs1-barcode-engine unit tests, symbols printed in GenSpecs 26.0 and the GS1 DataMatrix Guideline 2.5.1 (sampled from the PDFs), one oracle symbol per size, encodation-mode coverage, damage and orientation cases, Reed-Solomon vectors.
sources: GS1 General Specifications 26.0 (docs/specifications/gs1-general-specifications-v26.0.pdf), sections 4.14 and 5.6 (figures 4-3 to 4-15, 5-49 to 5-51; Tables 5-32, 5-33 page 380)
GS1 DataMatrix Guideline 2.5.1 (docs/specifications/gs1-datamatrix-guideline-v2.5.1.pdf), sections 1 to 4 and Annex A
bwip-js 4.11.4 (BWIPP 2026-05-28, MIT) and zxing-wasm 3.1.5 (zxing-cpp Apache-2.0, zint BSD-3-Clause) used as dev oracles

format.matrix: one string per module row, 'X' dark and ' ' light, no quiet zone (ModuleMatrix.fromRows input)
format.dataCodewords: data codewords up to (excluding) the first pad 129, after RS correction
format.rawData: what a reader transmits after aimId (FNC1 separators as GS 0x1D); for ECI symbols zxing transmits the converted text, see eci
format.encode: bit-exact: our GS1/DL encoder must reproduce matrix from the input (smallest size of the same shape). bit-exact-forced-size: same with the size forced. codewords-to-matrix: placement + padding + RS from dataCodewords at the given size must reproduce matrix. decode-only: decode must give aimId/rawData (encodation or padding differs from ours, or the matrix is damaged)
format.errorsCorrected: codewords corrected by an errors-only RS decoder (scratch decoder)

knownDisagreements: gs1-barcode-engine 289c899 pads with non-ISO values whenever the 253-state value exceeds 255 (it casts to uint8_t before testing > 254). Both engine vectors are affected; isoMatrix holds the ISO result, confirmed by bwip-js (GS1) and zint (Digital Link).
gs1-barcode-engine selectVersion starts at metrics[1], so it never emits 10x10, and it only reaches rectangular sizes when rows/columns are forced.

Guideline 2.5.1 Annex A Figure A-5 counts a "<Shift to alpha>" codeword; ASCII encodation has no such shift (uppercase letters are one codeword each), so the example needs 18, not 19, codewords and fits 18x18.

sizesSource: GS1 General Specifications 26.0 (docs/specifications/gs1-general-specifications-v26.0.pdf) Tables 5-32 and 5-33 (page 380) and gs1-barcode-engine master 289c899 (2024-09-26) dm.c metrics[]; all 30 verified against bwip-js 4.11.4

padding.rule: first pad 129; pad at 1-based position p: v = 129 + ((149*p) mod 253) + 1, minus 254 if v > 254

rs.generatorsNote: monic, highest-degree coefficient first (the leading 1 included). Validated indirectly: every size in symbols[] (all 30, all EC lengths) matches bwip-js bit for bit.

vectors.source: GS1 DataMatrix Guideline 2.5.1 (docs/specifications/gs1-datamatrix-guideline-v2.5.1.pdf), Annex A encoding example, pages 54-55

rs.qrNote: The same GF(2^8) code with polynomial 0x11D and roots from alpha^0 gives the ISO/IEC 18004 Annex I example (version 1-M, 01234567): data 16,32,12,86,97,128,236,17,236,17,236,17,236,17,236,17 -> EC 165,36,212,193,237,54,199,135,44,85 (computed by the scratch RS; matches the ISO example from memory; the QR research note owns this vector).
